The assistant provides a basic definition of a language model as a next-word predictor, which is correct but oversimplified. However, the answer to the second part—whether language models use labeled or unlabeled data—is inaccurate and confusing. Standard language model pre-training is self-supervised on vast amounts of **unlabeled** text; the "labels" (next tokens) are derived from the data itself, not from human annotation. Claiming that labeled data (with external annotations) is typically used to train a language model misrepresents the core methodology and could mislead non-technical customers. The response lacks depth, does not mention self-supervised learning, and fails to clarify the distinction in a trust-building way.

Rating: [[3]]
